h1: Outdoor Gym Equipment Manufacturer & Supplier in Shimla

h1Text: Outdoor Gym Equipment Manufacturer & Supplier in Shimla

richText.heading: Outdoor gym equipment supplier in Shimla

c: Snow, frost and steep slopes make Shimla one of the harder places to plan an open gym, and also one where people walk more than almost anywhere else. FunPlay Systems is an outdoor gym equipment supplier in Shimla for schools, colleges, government campuses, hotels and residential colonies in the Himachal Pradesh capital. We build our Fun Fitness range at our factory in Vasai, Maharashtra, about 1,370 km away, and bring it up by road.

Many Shimla schools are residential, with students on campus all year, so a few outdoor machines near the hostel or playing field get regular use. Hotels look at a small set for guests who want to exercise in the open air. In every case we start with photos and measurements of the flat area you have, then send a layout drawing before manufacture. Our team or a dealer in north India installs the machines.

richText.heading: Planning for cold winters and snow

c: Snow and freezing nights are hard on any outdoor equipment. Galvanised pipe frames do not rust when snow melts on them, and roto-moulded seats do not crack in the cold the way some painted surfaces chip. Before winter, have your staff tighten bolts and check that bearings turn freely.

items.q: Will snow damage outdoor gym machines in Shimla?
items.a: Snow by itself does not harm galvanised frames or moulded parts. Clear heavy snow from seats and moving parts, and avoid using the machines when they are iced over, as footplates become slippery.

items.q: Can you supply a residential school campus in Himachal Pradesh?
items.a: Yes. Send us the size of the open space and the age of the students. We will suggest machines that suit teenagers and staff and mark the clear space on a layout.

items.q: Who installs the equipment on hill sites?
items.a: Our installation team or a dealer in north India. The frames come in sections, so they can be carried to sites that trucks cannot reach directly.
